title: Mexican Fan Palm: Old Washingtonias You Can Visit
meta_description: The palace these seven palms were planted for came down in 1951. The palms did not. Five entries mapped in Porto, Granada, Palermo and Valencia.
intro: The building these palms were planted for was demolished in 1951 and the palms are still standing: seven Mexican fan palms in a line at the Palacio de Cristal in Porto, roughly 160 years old, outliving the glass hall they were meant to frame. That is the pattern with this species in Europe, which arrives as instant architecture and then outlasts it. Granada's four went up over the Plaza de Gracia in 1923, the year the palace behind them was finished. Palermo's line an avenue in the Villa Giulia, which opened in 1778 and is generally counted as Italy's first public garden. Valencia has two from the early twentieth century, one of them the result of a gardener's error that left it standing where it should not have been, taller and thinner than every palm around it.
